slice: A17 — health, jobs, audit, infrastructure and storage-GC dashboards reflect real operations
verdict: ADM-04 does NOT flip. Two of the seven observable criteria fail: the health dashboard cannot see a worker process at all (SC1), and job runs carry no correlation identity while the worker logs nothing for a failure (SC2). A17 stays OPEN.

prs.dependency_order: core #180 and user #177 are INDEPENDENT — neither changes api/openapi.yaml, so lib/api/generated.ts is untouched and there is no contract-ci ordering. The meta evidence PR lands last.
prs.migration: none — core stays at schema 132, search at 18

lab.topology: one origin — a pipe-only node proxy on 127.0.0.1:3100 in front of `node .next/standalone/server.js` on :3000 and vidra-core on :8088 — because vidra_refresh is SameSite=Lax, Path=/api/v1/auth
processes: vidra-core VIDRA_ROLE=worker — a real second process, no HTTP listener ('worker-only process ready; no HTTP listener in this role')
Next.js production standalone server behind the proxy
a compose `postgres:18-alpine` container, brought up only so deploy/backup.sh could run a REAL backup

lab.redis: native redis on 56379; core db 0, search db 1

lab.teardown: core api + worker, vidra-search, the Next server, the proxy, redis, postgres and the compose postgres container all stopped; lab directory, compose volume and this run's media objects removed. No lab artefact is committed.

degradations.search_stopped: killed at 00:43:51, degraded at 00:43:52 (< 1 s) with 'Get "http://127.0.0.1:8090/readyz": dial tcp ... connection refused'; restored and ok 4 s later. Chromium: Search DOWN.
degradations.settings_poller_broken: ALTER TABLE settings_version RENAME at 00:44:16; settings_sync down by 00:44:20 (< 1 poll interval) with 'the settings-version poll has been failing (last success 11s ago), so this replica may be serving stale instance settings/documents/branding: ERROR: relation "settings_version" does not exist (SQLSTATE 42P01)'. Renamed back at 00:44:58, ok by 00:45:03. Repeated in Chromium at 01:20:29-01:21:09 — the note renders, but only inside a `title` tooltip.
degradations.postgres_stopped: SEE THE DEFECT BELOW. Before the fix the whole page answered 401 'invalid or expired token'. After core#180 it answers 503 session_store_unavailable with the reason, and /readyz answers 503 'unavailable' as designed. The dashboard itself still cannot be READ during a full PostgreSQL outage — the read requires a session lookup — and /readyz remains the operator's fallback.

defect_found_and_fixed.what: requireAuth collapsed EVERY error from the per-request session lookup into 401 'invalid or expired token', including 'the database is unreachable'.
defect_found_and_fixed.measured: postgres stopped 00:45:52 -> GET /admin/system = 401 {"code":"unauthorized","message":"invalid or expired token"}
defect_found_and_fixed.consequence: the page whose job is to report the outage is the first page to stop answering, and every signed-in client is told its session is dead — a blip reads as a fleet-wide sign-out
defect_found_and_fixed.fix: core#180 — AuthenticateAccessToken separates pgx.ErrNoRows (the one answer that means the token no longer authorizes) from ErrSessionLookupUnavailable; requireAuth maps that to a typed SessionStoreUnavailableError -> 503 session_store_unavailable
defect_found_and_fixed.second_defect_in_the_fix: the first commit used a bare echo.NewHTTPError(503), and the central handler scrubs every 5xx message to 'an unexpected error occurred' unless a stable code is chosen first. Caught by running the fixed binary against the lab, not by the unit test. The test now asserts the sentence survives the scrubbing.
defect_found_and_fixed.verified_live: 503 {"code":"session_store_unavailable","message":"this server cannot reach its session store right now, so it cannot tell whether you are signed in. Your session is unaffected — retry shortly"}; the public GET /instance still answered 200 through the same outage; both recovered with no restart

settings_sync_worker_gap.status: REAL, UNCLOSED, and now measured rather than inferred
settings_sync_worker_gap.proof_a: the worker was killed at 00:45:23. /admin/system at 00:45:25 and 00:45:37 both reported status 'ok' with all seven components healthy. The dashboard has no component, no row and no hint that a worker process exists.
settings_sync_worker_gap.proof_b: during the 01:20:29-01:21:09 break the worker logged FIVE 'settings version poll failed; keeping the last known instance state' lines (01:20:29 / :39 / :49 / :59 / 01:21:09) and the API reported nothing about the worker at any point.
settings_sync_worker_gap.decision: NOT fixed in this slice, and the reason is a design ruling rather than effort. A per-process heartbeat is genuinely small at the API edge — SystemStatus.components is `additionalProperties` in api/openapi.yaml and AdminSystemStatusView humanises an unknown key (`key.replace(/_/g,' ')`), so a new component needs NO OpenAPI change and NO frontend change. What is not small is the STORE. A Redis key (SET vidra:settings-sync:<role>:<id> EX 3x interval, SCAN on read) needs no migration but puts the fleet's self-knowledge on a dependency that internal/settingsversion's own package comment argues against depending on; a `process_heartbeats` table (migration 0133 + two sqlc queries + wiring) is the house idiom but is a schema change for observability. Both are ~250-350 lines with tests, which is over this repo's one-small-PR bar on top of the two defects already fixed. Either mechanism must also be honest that it can only report a process alive enough to write a heartbeat: a crashed worker still shows as absence, not as failure.
settings_sync_worker_gap.recommended_shape: component key `settings_sync_peers`; not_configured when no store; ok when every peer heartbeat is fresh and error-free; down naming the roles/ids and reusing settingsSyncStatus's existing consequence sentence. Reuse the enabled/configured/note vocabulary from admin_infra.go rather than inventing a second one.

correlation_field_names_and_the_finding.http_layer: every request and every audit line carries `request_id` and `correlation_id` (X-Request-ID is echoed back as both X-Request-Id and X-Correlation-Id)
correlation_field_names_and_the_finding.audit_layer: audit_log rows carry request_id / correlation_id / trace_id / pipeline_run_id / job_id. Measured: 56 audit rows, 53 with a correlation_id. The admin retranscode wrote content.video.transcode with correlation_id 0C2BE25F-… — the exact X-Request-ID the browser sent.
correlation_field_names_and_the_finding.job_layer: job_runs and job_events carry pipeline_run_id / parent_job_id / actor_id / worker_id / request_id / correlation_id / trace_id / heartbeat_at / lease_expires_at columns — and NOTHING IN THE SHIPPED SCHEMA WRITES ANY OF THEM. The 0083 AFTER-trigger projection that maintains job_runs sets type/queue/source_id/state/stage/progress/attempt/actor/resource/error and no identity column; 0094, 0107, 0115 and 0120 add queues to the same projection and set none either. Measured over the whole table: 9 job_runs — 0 with worker_id, 0 with request_id, 0 with correlation_id, 0 with trace_id, 0 with pipeline_run_id; 53 job_events — 0 with worker_id, 0 with correlation_id. And audit_log.job_id is populated on 0 of 56 rows, so the audit row does not link forward either.
correlation_field_names_and_the_finding.ui_consequence: AdminJobRunsView's detail panel read, in Chromium, on the dead-lettered transcode: Pipeline run —, Parent job —, Actor —, Worker —, Request ID —, Correlation ID —, Trace ID —, Claimed —, Heartbeat —, Lease expires —. The table's WORKER column is '—' on all seven rows and ?worker_id=<anything> returns total 0.
correlation_field_names_and_the_finding.log_consequence: the WORKER PROCESS LOGGED NOTHING for any of the three failures. Its last WARN/ERROR was a boot line; across the whole run its only job lines are 'transcode drain completed jobs count=1' and 'upload finalize drain completed jobs count=1'. grep for the admin request's correlation id: 2 hits in the api log (the audit line and the request line), 0 in the worker log.
correlation_field_names_and_the_finding.sharpest_form: the run detail's own error_detail says 'Execution failed; inspect correlated system logs for diagnostic detail.' — pointing an operator at logs that (a) carry no correlation id for this run and (b) contain no line about this failure at all.

retry.seam: there is NO retry control on the jobs page. The shipped retry is POST /admin/videos/{id}/transcoding, reachable from the kebab on AdminVideosView and VideoActionsMenu ('HLS transcoding queued.' / 'Web Video transcoding queued.').
retry.creates_a_new_run: proven — a new transcode_jobs row e24c032e with its own job_runs projection, alongside the still-visible dead-lettered 3679487c
retry.idempotent_re_retry: a second POST while one is in flight is 409 'a transcode job is already in progress for this video'
retry.fixed_input_succeeds: the original object was restored and the retried job completed on attempt 0; the queue row reads done att=0 and a new video_transcode_hls run succeeded at 01:13:29

sc2_failed_job_correlation_retry.gap_channel_syncs: channel_syncs is deliberately NOT projected into job_runs (the 0083 header lists it among the tables that 'need distinct execution rows before they can be represented honestly') and it has no queue row in GET /admin/jobs. Measured: 1 channel_syncs row in state=failed, 0 job_runs rows with queue='channel_syncs', 7 queues on the dashboard. A failing channel sync is visible only to the channel owner via GET /channel-syncs — the operator has no surface for it at all.

The list VIEW renders only action / result / relative time / actor / reason — resource, correlation id, metadata and changes are returned by the API and dropped by the UI.

In Chromium a signed-in MODERATOR gets 'Administrators only. This page is for administrators.' on /admin/audit-log and /admin/jobs while /moderation renders for the same session.

sc4_storage_and_media_gc.verdict: PASS for media GC; the storage-migration live facet is UNVERIFIED (one backend in the lab)
sc4_storage_and_media_gc.gate_semantics_as_shipped: MEDIA_GC_ENABLED is boot-baked (it is NOT an instance-settings key — PATCH media_gc_enabled is 422 'unknown setting') and it gates the DAILY sweep ONLY. internal/httpapi/admin_media.go says so: 'The manual POST stays mounted either way — an operator asking for a sweep by hand is not the hazard the flag exists for.' Verified by experiment: with MEDIA_GC_ENABLED=false, GET /admin/media/gc reports enabled=false and POST {"dry_run": false} answered 200, mode=delete, deleted=1, and the planted orphan was gone from disk. The brief's expected 'off -> refused' is NOT the shipped contract.
sc4_storage_and_media_gc.ui_consequence_fixed: the panel rendered 'Automatic daily sweep: Off' beside a fully armed purge button, above a paragraph that only describes what happens when GC is ENABLED. user#177 adds one warning line when the flag is off; the button deliberately stays live.
sc4_storage_and_media_gc.real_pass_with_counts: on a clean store of 20 objects with one planted orphan: dry run -> scanned 20, orphans 1, orphan_percent 5, deleted 0; destructive -> mode=delete, deleted 1, file gone. Driven end to end in Chromium: Run dry run -> 'Scanned 20 stored objects — 1 orphan to delete — Storage: local disk' with the key listed -> 'Purge 1 orphan' -> 'This permanently deletes the 1 object listed above… Type PURGE to confirm' -> deleted, and audited as admin.media.gc success reason 'mode=delete scanned=20 orphans=1 orphan_pct=5 deleted=1 breaker=false ownership=not-applicable forced_dry_run=false forced_reason=none'.
sc4_storage_and_media_gc.breaker: on the pre-existing dev store (221 objects, 203 orphans) a requested destructive sweep was DOWNGRADED, not failed: dry_run=true, mode=dry-run, orphan_percent=91, breaker_tripped=true, deleted=0, with the full orphan list still returned so the operator can decide. max_orphan_percent 25.
sc4_storage_and_media_gc.scheduled_sweep: the worker's own daily sweep is on the same dashboard: 'media gc sweep completed mode=dry-run scanned=221 orphans=203 orphan_percent=91 …' and an admin.media.gc audit row with actor '—'. The first sweep after each boot is always a dry run.
sc4_storage_and_media_gc.storage_migrations: GET /admin/storage/migrations -> {"migrations":[]} (200); GET /admin/storage/migrations/{unknown} -> 404 'no such storage migration'; POST /admin/storage/migrations on a local-only deployment -> 503. The live facet (a real bounded migration) is UNVERIFIED — the lab has one backend and no S3 credentials. Blocker: a second storage backend.
sc4_storage_and_media_gc.defect_recorded: that 503 answers {"code":"service_unavailable","message":"an unexpected error occurred"} — the 5xx message scrubber again, the same class core#180 fixes for sessions. The admin is told nothing; the REASON survives only in the audit trail, as admin.storage.migration.start FAILURE reason=no_target_configured. A typed error with a stable code would put it in the response.
sc4_storage_and_media_gc.authorization: GET and POST /admin/media/gc and /admin/storage/migrations: moderator 403, ordinary user 403, anonymous 401.

findings_for_the_backlog: job_runs / job_events identity columns are written by nothing (worker_id, request_id, correlation_id, trace_id, pipeline_run_id, heartbeat_at, lease_expires_at). The contract, the UI detail panel, the table's Worker column and the worker_id filter all exist over columns that are structurally always empty. Closing it means threading the request context into the queue tables and the 0083 trigger — a schema + every-enqueue-path change, not a surgical one.
the worker process logs NOTHING for a failed job. Three real failures across three queues produced zero WARN/ERROR lines on the worker.
the two together make the run detail's own advice — 'inspect correlated system logs for diagnostic detail' — impossible to follow.
channel_syncs has no operator surface at all: not projected into job_runs, no queue row on /admin/jobs.
a corrupt upload fails the VIDEO and no job, so it leaves nothing on the jobs dashboard (deliberate, documented in uploadfinalize).
the postgres and redis probes on /admin/system are not bounded by systemProbeTimeout; a refused redis dial cost 3.4-5.2 s of page latency and a hung one would hang the page.
an authorization refusal (403/401 on an admin route) writes no audit row.
